# PM

> PM is a single-binary process manager for macOS/Linux. It runs a resident
> daemon, exposes a Unix-socket control API and an optional local web console,
> and keeps all default data under `~/.pm`. This file is the complete, offline
> guide an AI agent needs to use and configure PM. Run `pm llms.txt` to print it.

PM does not depend on a database, Node.js, or an external web server. The web
console's static assets are embedded in the binary. No telemetry is collected.

## Quick start

```bash
make install            # or: go install ./cmd/pm   (needs Go 1.26+)
pm daemon -d            # start the daemon in the background (or run under launchd/systemd)
sudo pm systemd         # Linux: install, enable at boot, and start pm.service
pm update               # update this binary from the latest GitHub release
pm list                 # compact list of managed processes
pm status               # detailed table (CPU, memory, uptime, restarts, exit)
```

On the first run, PM creates `~/.pm/` and writes a default, editable config to
`~/.pm/pm.yaml`. With the default config the web console is enabled at
http://127.0.0.1:19090 (token optional while listening on loopback).

All default data lives under `~/.pm`:

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.pm/pm.yaml` | configuration (auto-generated on first run) |
| `~/.pm/pm.sock` | Unix control socket |
| `~/.pm/events.jsonl` | lifecycle event history |
| `~/.pm/program-state.json` | persistent pause/disable markers |
| `~/.pm/logs/pm-daemon.log` | daemon log when started with `-d` |
| `~/.pm/logs/<name>.log` | a managed process' stdout/stderr (when configured) |

To override the config location, pass `-config FILE`. A `pm.yaml` in the current
directory takes priority over `~/.pm/pm.yaml` when `-config` is omitted.

## Commands

```
pm [-socket PATH] daemon [-config FILE] [-d] [-log FILE]
pm [-socket PATH] up [-config FILE] [-d] [-log FILE]  # alias for daemon
pm systemd [-config FILE]                    # Linux system service installation (run with sudo)
pm update                                      # download and install latest GitHub release
pm [-socket PATH] status [NAME...]        # full details for all or named programs
pm [-socket PATH] list   [NAME...]        # compact overview including PID, TCP ports and uptime
pm [-socket PATH] start|stop|restart NAME|all
pm [-socket PATH] pause|resume|disable|enable NAME|all
pm [-socket PATH] reload                  # hot-reload program config from disk
pm [-socket PATH] shutdown                # stop the daemon (and all managed programs)
pm [-socket PATH] down                    # alias for shutdown
pm [-socket PATH] logs [-n LINES] [-f] [-stderr] NAME
pm llms.txt                               # print this guide
pm version
```

`status` shows full detail (state, PID, TCP listening ports, CPU, memory,
child/descendant process counts, Go goroutines when configured, uptime, start
count, exit code, last error). `list` is a compact quick overview. Process actions accept several
names or the literal `all`. `stop` is temporary: an autostart program starts
again after a daemon restart. `pause` and `disable` persist their markers and
prevent autostart; `resume` and `enable` clear the corresponding marker and
start the program immediately.

`restart` validates and re-reads `pm.yaml` before stopping the selected
programs, so changes to environment variables, arguments, and log paths take
effect on the new process. An invalid configuration leaves the running process
untouched. Use `reload` to add or remove programs.

On Linux, `sudo pm systemd` installs the current binary as
`/usr/local/bin/pm`, writes `/etc/systemd/system/pm.service`, enables it at boot,
and hands an existing daemon over to systemd. The service runs as the original
sudo user and uses a current-directory `pm.yaml` when present, otherwise that
user's `~/.pm/pm.yaml`. Pass `-config FILE` to choose another file.

`pm update` queries the latest stable GitHub Release. If its tag equals the
compiled-in current version, no files are downloaded. Otherwise PM downloads
the matching `pm-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` asset, verifies its GitHub SHA-256 digest
(falling back to `SHA256SUMS` and legacy raw assets for older releases), safely
extracts the executable, checks its reported version, then atomically replaces
the current executable. Use `sudo pm update` when it is installed in a
root-owned directory. Manually downloaded archives contain `pm` with mode
`0755`, so `tar -xzf pm-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` needs no subsequent `chmod`.
A running daemon keeps the old code until it is restarted. After an interactive
update, an active systemd-managed pm.service prompts for an immediate restart;
non-interactive updates print the restart command instead. Restarting PM stops
all managed programs, then starts only autostart programs that are neither
paused nor disabled. Detached daemons must be restarted with `pm down` followed
by `pm up -d`.

CLI socket resolution order: `-socket PATH` flag → `PM_SOCKET` env → `socket`
field from the config → `~/.pm/pm.sock`.

## Configuration

Config is YAML. Relative paths resolve against the config file's directory
(`~/.pm` by default). Unknown fields are rejected. Strict validation runs on
load and on web edits; the daemon refuses to start on invalid config.

### Daemon fields

| Field | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `socket` | CLI control socket | `pm.sock` (→ `~/.pm/pm.sock`) |
| `state_dir` | runtime state dir (events) | `.` (→ `~/.pm`) |
| `event_history` | events kept in memory; `0` disables | `1000` |
| `web.enabled` | enable the HTTP console | `true` |
| `web.listen` | HTTP listen address | `127.0.0.1:19090` |
| `web.token` | access token, literal | empty |
| `web.token_env` | env var name holding the token (preferred) | empty |

### Program fields

| Field | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | unique program name; no whitespace (Unicode such as CJK is allowed) | required |
| `description` | optional note/summary; no newlines, max 256 chars | empty |
| `group` | grouping for filtering | `default` |
| `command` | executable; NOT parsed by a shell | required |
| `args` | argument list | `[]` |
| `directory` | working directory | daemon's cwd |
| `environment` | env vars to add/override | `{}` |
| `autostart` | start when the daemon starts | `true` |
| `restart` | `never` / `unexpected` / `always` | `unexpected` |
| `restart_delay` | wait before auto-restart | `1s` |
| `max_restarts` | max restarts in the window; `0` = unlimited | `5` |
| `restart_window` | restart-count window | `1m` |
| `stop_signal` | `TERM` / `INT` / `QUIT` / `HUP` | `TERM` |
| `stop_timeout` | grace period before force-killing the tree | `10s` |
| `stdout_log` | stdout log path | inherits daemon output |
| `stderr_log` | stderr log path (may equal stdout_log) | inherits daemon output |
| `log_max_bytes` | per-file rotation threshold; `0` = no rotation | `10485760` |
| `log_backups` | rotated backups to keep | `3` |
| `pprof_url` | Go pprof base URL for goroutine count | empty (disabled) |

Child and descendant counts are collected automatically from OS process
relationships. TCP metrics contain only listening ports and include sockets
owned by the managed process or any of its descendants. For a Go program,
expose `net/http/pprof` on a loopback-only
listener and set, for example,
`pprof_url: http://127.0.0.1:6060/debug/pprof`. PM reads the goroutine profile
with a 750ms timeout. Do not expose pprof directly to the public internet.

Restart semantics: `unexpected` restarts only on non-zero exit; `always`
restarts on any exit; `never` does not. Too many restarts within
`restart_window` push the program into `FATAL`. `command` is not shell-parsed —
for pipes/redirection/loops use `command: /bin/sh` and `args: ["-c", "..."]`.

### Example

```yaml
socket: pm.sock
state_dir: .
event_history: 1000

web:
  enabled: true
  listen: 127.0.0.1:19090

programs:
  - name: example-worker
    description: example program printing a heartbeat every 5s
    group: workers
    command: /bin/sh
    args: ["-c", 'while true; do echo "tick $(date)"; sleep 5; done']
    directory: "."
    environment:
      APP_ENV: local
    autostart: true
    restart: unexpected
    restart_delay: 1s
    max_restarts: 5
    restart_window: 1m
    stop_signal: TERM
    stop_timeout: 10s
    stdout_log: logs/example-worker.log
    stderr_log: logs/example-worker.error.log
    pprof_url: http://127.0.0.1:6060/debug/pprof
    log_max_bytes: 10485760
    log_backups: 3
```

## Web security

Set `web.enabled: false` to disable HTTP entirely; the Unix-socket CLI is
unaffected. The default listener is loopback only, where a token is optional.
Listening beyond loopback (`0.0.0.0`, etc.) REQUIRES `token` or `token_env` or
the daemon refuses to start. Prefer injecting the token via an env var:

```yaml
web:
  enabled: true
  listen: 0.0.0.0:19090
  token_env: PM_WEB_TOKEN
```
```bash
export PM_WEB_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
```

Tokens travel in cleartext over HTTP on a LAN — put HTTPS (reverse proxy) or an
SSH tunnel in front for cross-machine access: `ssh -L 19090:127.0.0.1:19090 user@host`.

## reload vs restart

`pm reload` re-reads `~/.pm/pm.yaml` and applies a DIFFERENTIAL update: unchanged
programs keep their PID; only added/removed/changed programs are affected, and
merely changing a `group` does not restart a program. Changes to `socket`,
`web`, `state_dir`, or `event_history` are NOT hot-applicable and require a
daemon restart (`pm shutdown` then `pm daemon`).

The web console edits config safely: it writes `<config>.bak`, then atomically
replaces the config via a temp file in the same directory.

## Common tasks for agents

- Add a process: append a program entry to `~/.pm/pm.yaml`, then `pm reload`.
  To manage it without reloading other programs, the differential reload keeps
  existing PIDs stable.
- Tail logs: `pm logs -f -n 200 NAME` (stdout); add `-stderr` for stderr.
- Check health: `pm list` for a fast scan, `pm status NAME` for detail.
- Stop everything: `pm stop all`. Stop the daemon: `pm shutdown`.
- Keep a program stopped across daemon or machine restarts: `pm pause NAME`;
  use `pm resume NAME` to allow and start it again. Use `disable`/`enable` for
  the stronger administrative marker.
- Diagnose a `FATAL` program: `pm status NAME` shows restart count and last
  error; review `~/.pm/logs/<name>.log` and `~/.pm/logs/pm-daemon.log`.
- Move data: edit `~/.pm/pm.yaml` paths, or run with `-config` pointing
  elsewhere; remember `socket`/`state_dir`/`web`/`event_history` changes need a
  daemon restart, not just `reload`.

## Notes

- Stateful data is plain files under `~/.pm`; back up or inspect directly.
- Long-running deployments should use launchd (macOS) or systemd (Linux), not
  `-d`. On Linux use `sudo pm systemd`; see `deploy/` for advanced dedicated-user
  templates. When managed by the OS, do not pass `-d`.
- `pm llms.txt` works offline and needs no running daemon.
